pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we read different types of materials?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING
This lesson teaches Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading for Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading above.
2. Explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read different types of materials?
2. What kind of materials do you enjoy reading?
3. What can you do to remember what you read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for lifelong learning
2. demonstrate independent reading of a variety of materials (narratives, poems, graded readers) for information

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
